title: forces-1d-v1
learningObjectives: Simplified motion isolates one direction with opposing forces balanced while examining a single net force
Constant velocity is maintained when opposing forces balance; unbalanced force causes motion in the direction of the larger force
Acceleration is determined by net force divided by mass as expressed by a = F_net / m

sources.title: Simplified Aircraft Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

explanations.text: Balanced opposing forces maintain steady motion, while an unbalanced force drives motion in the direction of the larger force.

evidence.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust
If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

explanations.text: Net force is the difference between opposing forces such as thrust minus drag or lift minus weight, and it determines the resulting acceleration.

evidence.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

explanations.text: When second-law dynamics are applied, the aircraft's acceleration can be calculated from net force and mass.

evidence.quote: We can compute the acceleration which the aircraft will experience from Newton’s second law of motion
Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

behavioralTests.name: Positive net force produces positive acceleration
Negative net force produces negative acceleration
Zero net force yields zero acceleration
